About this skill

What it does

Turns competitor research into a decision, not a summary: classifies each priority competitor on two axes (market mindshare and resource strength dedicated to the market) into one of five categories -- all-out attack, monitor, harvest, ignore, or partner -- each mapped to a specific playbook of moves, then names one primary motion, an owner, and a trigger per player. Runs reconnaissance (unaided-before-aided customer-view signal collection across messaging, pricing, hiring/funding, SEO, and reviews), extraction questions per competitor, matrix placement with rationale and confidence, playbook selection, and an optional market-shape read (fragmented/challenger/ancient/mature). Includes a completion gate that blocks a 'research only' handoff with no attached decision.

Use when

  • competitor analysis
  • market mapping
  • GTM prioritisation
  • build a battlecard
  • market intelligence review

Works on

  • a market/category and the priority competitors to evaluate
  • publicly observable competitor signals (site messaging, pricing, ads, reviews, hiring/funding, SEO)

Produces

  • a competitor map (direct/adjacent/substitute/ecosystem)
  • a matrix placement per competitor with rationale and confidence
  • one primary playbook motion, owner, and trigger per priority competitor
  • an optional market-shape read and whitespace/positioning notes

Instructions

The full text of SKILL.md, as the agent reads it.

Market Command Matrix

Goal: intelligence upstream of action—not competitor summaries for their own sake. Classify players, decide what to do, assign owners and triggers.

The model (two axes)

Market mindshare — awareness, conversation, category association, unprompted recall, default comparisons when buyers think about the problem.

Resource strength — capacity and focus dedicated to winning this market (funding, team, distribution, tech, partnerships, operational depth). Score relative to market dedication, not raw company size. Practical approach: score your own company 1–5 on focus and execution in this market, then score others relative to you.

Each axis: high / medium / low (justify with evidence).

Decision categories

CategoryTypical placementOne-line intent
All-out attackHigh mindshare + high resourcesSharp wedge, proof, channel discipline; expect retaliation.
MonitorLow mindshare + high resourcesWatch capacity; triggers before overreacting.
HarvestHigh mindshare + low resourcesUse their awareness; win on fulfilment, trust, depth, migration paths.
IgnoreLow mindshare + low resourcesNo strategic energy; note customer signals only.
PartnerComplementary / ecosystemIntegration, referral, co-marketing, bundling—define value exchange; watch channel conflict.

Partner is orthogonal to the 2×2; label when beating them is not required to win.

Competitor set (before matrix placement)

Classify the map from the customer view of the market (buckets inform discovery; matrix uses mindshare + resources):

  1. Direct — same buyer, same JTBD, comparable promise; same budget or decision.
  2. Adjacent — overlapping workflow; could expand into your lane; partner and/or threat.
  3. Substitute behaviours — manual, informal, “good enough” habits instead of buying.
  4. Ecosystem — media, communities, platforms, agencies, infra that shape trust and access.

Workflow (run in order)

1. Reconnaissance

  • Prefer customer-led signals: core unaided question first: When you think of [CATEGORY], what is the first product that comes to mind? Then aided recognition, usage, recommendation, value/friction.
  • Bias controls: unaided before aided; neutral framing where possible; separate verified evidence from assumptions.
  • Collect current signals per priority player (site messaging, product claims, social themes, ads, reviews, pricing/onboarding, press/partnerships, hiring/funding, SEO topics, FAQs/objections). Full list: reference.md.

2. Monitoring and extraction

For each priority player, extract meaning: promise, ICP, lead pain, proof, CTA, strongest channel, what they avoid saying, visible operational weakness, behaviour they try to change. Questions: reference.md.

3. Matrix placement

For each player: category, rationale, confidence (high/medium/low), evidence used, what would change the placement.

4. Playbook selection

One primary motion per priority player. Do not output a dump without decisions. Playbook menus: reference.md.

5. Market shape

With enough coverage: fragmented | challenger | ancient | mature—and what that implies for offence vs defence. Definitions: reference.md.

6. Whitespace and positioning

Turn gaps into actions: underserved audience, weak promise, missing proof, poor follow-through, trust gap, channel mismatch, etc.

Output formats

  • Full analysis: strategic thesis, competitor map, evidence table, matrix placement, whitespace, recommended actions (owner, dependency, output, deadline), market shape, milestones/triggers. Skeleton: reference.md.
  • One-page memo (compressed): Player → Placement → Evidence (1–2 signals) → Meaning → Action → Trigger.

Use format:one-page in the user request when they need the short memo only.

Completion gate (do not “finalize” without)

  • Competitor set classified (direct / adjacent / substitute / ecosystem as relevant).
  • Matrix category per priority player + rationale + confidence.
  • Evidence vs assumptions separated.
  • One selected primary playbook motion per priority player + next action + checkpoint or trigger.
  • Market-shape interpretation if enough players/data exist.
  • No “research only” handoff—every section ties to a decision or motion.
